assumptions.condition: The pair \(\mathcal{A}_{0,P},\mathcal{A}_{1,P}\) is a measurable partition of \(\mathcal{X}_P\) up to the boundary convention, and \(\mathcal{B}_P\) is its common relative interface.

standard.name: random-design density bounded away from zero and infinity
conditional variance bounded away from zero and infinity

assumptions.condition: \(P\{X\in\mathcal E_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}=P\{T=t,\ X\in B_2(x,r)\}\geq c_{-}r^2\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<r\leq r_0\).

novel.justification: This inspectable actual-arm condition holds when both realized assignment arms satisfy a uniform interior-cone or corkscrew condition at the known interface under a score density bounded below locally. It excludes cusps, vanishing wedges, and arms that pinch out, and is load-bearing for stable coordinatewise distance estimation.

The novel tag records provenance only because the schema requires a standard-or-novel classification; this routine quantitative uniform geometric regularity restriction is not claimed as an original contribution. An injective \(C^{\iota+2}\) embedding covers smooth non-self-intersecting boundaries represented by geographic-information-system or spline charts, and it defines the smooth subclass and its trimmed chart.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal{X}_P=[-1,1]^2\), \(\gamma_P(u)=(2u-1,0)\), \(\mathcal{A}_{0,P}=\{z\in\mathcal{X}_P:z_2<0\}\), and \(\mathcal{A}_{1,P}=\{z\in\mathcal{X}_P:z_2\geq0\}\), with the displayed convention on the interface.
The law of \(X\) under \(P\) is absolutely continuous with respect to two-dimensional Lebesgue measure, with density \(f_P\) supported on \(\mathcal X_P\).

novel.justification: standard: absolute continuity of a random-design law with respect to Lebesgue measure

assumptions.condition: \(f_P(x)\leq L\) for two-dimensional Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

definitions.name: D_{P,x}
definitions.construction: \[D_{P,x}=(2T-1)\lVert X-x\rVert_2,\qquad x\in\mathcal{B}_P.\]

definitions.name: U_{n,P}(x)
definitions.construction: \[U_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n),\qquad x\in\mathcal{B}_P.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{dist}}_n
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{dist}}_n=\left\{\widehat{\tau}_n:\widehat{\tau}_n(x)=T_{n,x}(U_{n,P}(x))\text{ for a measurable }T_{n,x}\text{ at every }x\in\mathcal{B}_P\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{loc}}_n
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{loc}}_n=\left\{\widetilde{\tau}_n:\widetilde{\tau}_n(\cdot)=L_n(O_{1:n},\mathcal{A}_{0,P},\mathcal{A}_{1,P},\mathcal{B}_P)\text{ for a jointly measurable }L_n\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}(q,L,c_{-},r_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}=\left\{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}:P\text{ satisfies all member properties enumerated below}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}=\gamma_P([\delta,1-\delta]),\qquad0<\delta<1/2.\]

definitions.name: K_\triangle
definitions.construction: \[K_\triangle(u)=\max\{1-|u|,0\}.\] This fixed kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, Lipschitz, supported on \([-1,1]\), and positive on \((-1,1)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}
definitions.construction: Coarea angular-density confounding handle: expand each arm-specific radial conditional mean as a ratio of circle-level angular integrals; vary bounded continuous score densities through shrinking-scale angular imbalances while preserving the fixed radial mass envelope; pair those imbalances with disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines and bounded or Bernoulli outcomes; and use the induced compressed likelihoods to determine both a separated-center packing and the primitive regularity that prevents such confounding.

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction:
Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), a cutoff constant \(c>0\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Put \(v_m(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{m-1})^\top\), let \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), and set \(S_{P,x,i}=|D_{P,x,i}|\).  At the probability-zero value \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), assign the observation to neither arm.  Define
\[
 \widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
Let
\[
 G_m=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad \lambda_m(c)=c\lambda_{\min}(G_m),
\]
and define the stabilized arm intercept and arm difference by
\[
 \widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h),
 &\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}\geq\lambda_m(c)/2,\\
 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}<\lambda_m(c)/2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{1,h,c}(x)
 -\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{0,h,c}(x).
\]
The cutoff input \(c\) is suppressed from the notation for \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\).  The formula is defined for every \(h>0\); in an order-\(m\) coarea class it is used with \(c=\underline c\) and \(0<h\leq r_*\).  The strict sign convention, eigenvalue cutoff, inverse branch, and zero branch make this a pointwise Borel formula of \(U_{n,P}(x)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{coarea}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb N,\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{E}_{t,P}
definitions.construction:
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the observed assignment arm
\[
 \mathcal E_{t,P}
 =\left\{z\in\mathcal X_P:
 \mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_{1,P}\}=t\right\}.
\]
The assignment-partition convention makes these two sets a measurable partition of \(\mathcal X_P\), and deterministic assignment gives
\[
 \mathbf 1\{T=t\}=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal E_{t,P}\}
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]

definitions.name: Q_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction:
Fix \(x\in\mathcal B_P\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).  On the Borel subsets \(A\) of \((0,\infty)\), define the finite observable radial measure
\[
 \nu_{t,P,x}(A)
 =P\{T=t,\ \lVert X-x\rVert_2\in A\}.
\]
Score absolute continuity and polar coarea imply \(\nu_{t,P,x}\ll ds\).  Define \(Q_{t,P,x}:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) to be one fixed finite Borel-measurable Radon--Nikodym version
\[
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\frac{d\nu_{t,P,x}}{ds}(s).
\]
For Lebesgue-almost every radial index \(s>0\), this fixed version agrees with the coarea identity
\[
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap\mathcal E_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P}
 f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z).
\]
No equality with the displayed circle integral is stipulated at exceptional radii.

definitions.name: N_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction:
Fix \(x\in\mathcal B_P\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and suppose \(\mathbb E_P|Y|<\infty\).  On the Borel subsets \(A\) of \((0,\infty)\), define the finite signed observable radial measure
\[
 \zeta_{t,P,x}(A)
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf 1\{T=t,\ \lVert X-x\rVert_2\in A\}\right].
\]
Consistency, deterministic assignment, and score absolute continuity imply \(\zeta_{t,P,x}\ll ds\).  Define \(N_{t,P,x}:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) to be one fixed finite Borel-measurable Radon--Nikodym version
\[
 N_{t,P,x}(s)=\frac{d\zeta_{t,P,x}}{ds}(s).
\]
For Lebesgue-almost every radial index \(s>0\), this fixed version agrees with the coarea identity
\[
 N_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap\mathcal E_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P}
 \mu_{t,P}(z)f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z).
\]
No equality with the displayed circle integral is stipulated at exceptional radii.

definitions.name: \mathcal{S}_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction:
For \(x\in\mathcal B_P\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the positive-Radon--Nikodym radius domain
\[
 \mathcal S_{t,P,x}=\{s\in(0,\infty):Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\}.
\]
It is defined only up to a Lebesgue-null modification inherited from the fixed version of \(Q_{t,P,x}\), and all essential-limit statements are invariant to such modifications.

definitions.name: g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction:
For \(x\in\mathcal B_P\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the partial observed exact-distance regression only on \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) by
\[
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)},
 \qquad s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}.
\]
No value is defined at \(s=0\) or at a radius for which \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=0\).

definitions.name: \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}
definitions.construction:
Suppose zero belongs to the essential support of the observed radial measure \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\), meaning
\[
 \int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds>0
 \quad\text{for every }r>0.
\]
Define \(\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)\) to be the essential limit of the partial observed regression at zero, relative to that radial measure,
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)
 =\mathop{\operatorname{ess\,lim}}_{s\downarrow0,\ s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}}^{Q_{t,P,x}(s)ds}
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s),
\]
whenever there is a unique \(a\in\mathbb R\) such that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some \(r>0\) satisfies
\[
 \int_{(0,r)\cap\mathcal S_{t,P,x}}
 \mathbf 1\{|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-a|>\varepsilon\}
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds=0.
\]
The two treatment arms have separate essential limits; no common radius sequence is part of the definition.

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal I_q=\{\alpha=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\in\mathbb N_0^2:|\alpha|\leq q-1\}\), let \(p_q=|\mathcal I_q|\), and let \(r_q(u)=(u^\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I_q)^\top\), ordered with the constant monomial first.  Put \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\) and
\[
 K_2(u)=(1-\lVert u\rVert_2)_+,
 \qquad H_t=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:(2t-1)u_2>0\}.
\]
Define the deterministic half-ball reference matrix and cutoff by
\[
 G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}
 =L^{-1}\int_{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)}
 K_2(u)r_q(u)r_q(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad
 \lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}
 =\lambda_{\min}(G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}).
\]
For \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(h>0\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), put \(U_{x,i}=(X_i-x)/h\) and define
\[
 \widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}K_2(U_{x,i})r_q(U_{x,i})r_q(U_{x,i})^\top,
\]
\[
 \widehat r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}K_2(U_{x,i})r_q(U_{x,i})Y_i.
\]
The stabilized arm intercept is
\[
 \widehat\mu^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}
 \widehat r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h),
 &\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)\}
 \geq\lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}/2,\\
 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)\}
 <\lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}/2,
 \end{cases}
\]
and the fitted-intercept difference is
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{1,h}(x)
 -\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{0,h}(x).
\]
Finite sums, the eigenvalue cutoff, matrix inversion on the positive-definite branch, and the zero failure branch make this a jointly Borel map of the full sample and known assignment geometry.

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{NP}}
definitions.construction:
\[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)=\bigl\{P:\text{conditions (i)--(iv) below hold}\bigr\}.\]
Condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\): for every \(n\), \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independently and identically distributed under \(P\) in \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\): \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on its compact support \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), with \(L^{-1}\leq\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq L\), and \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a rectifiable curve.  Condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\): \(\mu_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\): \(\sigma_P^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\) and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma_P^2(x)\leq L\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

definitions.name: V_{n,P}(x)
definitions.construction: \[V_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n),\qquad x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P).\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{NP}}_n
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}=\left\{\widehat\mu_n:\widehat\mu_n(x)=T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))\text{ for a measurable }T_{n,x}\text{ selected independently of }P\text{ at every }x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\right\}.\]

definitions.name: R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}
definitions.construction: \[R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}=\inf_{\widehat\mu_n\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)}\mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}|\widehat\mu_n(x)-\mu_P(x)|\right].\]
