statements.statement: For the fixed kernel \(K_\triangle\), there is \(\kappa_0=\kappa_0(c_{-},r_0)>0\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(h\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_P}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0,\qquad \inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0.\]
statements.justification: This theorem-local support verifies denominator stability for the one fixed degree-zero estimator used in both distance upper bounds.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance uses a broader high-level Gram condition for local-polynomial upper theory; this lemma derives only the scalar bound needed by the fixed triangular local-constant estimator.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable and smooth distance upper bounds use the same stable estimator without quantifying over kernels or polynomial degrees.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\) in either displayed class, an arm \(t\), and a point \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Put \(R_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2\).  Symmetry of the triangular kernel and the signed-distance definition give
\[
 K_\triangle(D_{P,x}/h)=K_\triangle(R_x/h).
\]
Moreover, \(K_\triangle(u)\geq1/2\) for \(0\leq u\leq1/2\).  Therefore, whenever \(0<h\leq2r_0\), actual-arm thickness yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)
 &=h^{-2}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 K_\triangle(R_x/h)\mathbf1\{T=t\}\right]\\
 &\geq \frac1{2h^2}P\{T=t,\ R_x\leq h/2\}\\
 &\geq \frac1{2h^2}c_-(h/2)^2
 =\frac{c_-}{8}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The thickness hypothesis is uniform in \(P,t,x\).  For the smooth class, \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\subseteq\mathcal B_P\), so the same calculation applies on the trimmed boundary.  Thus one may take \(\kappa_0=c_-/8\), with ``sufficiently small'' meaning \(h\leq2r_0\).

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cup\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P\{T=t,\ \lVert X-x\rVert_2\leq r\}
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
 \geq c_-r^2,
 \qquad 0<r\leq r_0.
\]
Thus zero belongs to the essential support of each observed arm-specific radial measure.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
 =\mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s].
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls
\]
for \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\)-almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  Consequently the separate essential arm limit exists and satisfies
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x),
 \qquad
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]
No value at \(s=0\) or at a zero-denominator radius, and no radius sequence common to the two arms, is used.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\), \(x\), and \(t\) as displayed, and put \(R_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2\).  By the definition of the observable radial measure and its fixed Radon--Nikodym density,
\[
 P\{T=t,\ 0<R_x\leq r\}
 =\nu_{t,P,x}((0,r])
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
Score absolute continuity gives \(P(R_x=0)=0\).  The actual-arm thickness condition bounds the last display below by \(c_-r^2\) for \(0<r\leq r_0\).  Therefore every neighborhood \((0,r]\) has positive \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)ds\)-measure.  This is exactly the assertion that zero belongs to the essential support; it makes no topological claim about a particular representative's pointwise positive set.

For every bounded Borel function \(a:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), the defining Radon--Nikodym identities give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(R_x)]
 =\int_0^\infty a(s)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(R_x)]
 =\int_0^\infty a(s)N_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
The class's conditional sub-Gaussian condition and H\"older envelope imply \(\mathbb E_P|Y|<\infty\).  Because \(P(R_x=0)=0\), the sign of \(D_{P,x}=(2T-1)R_x\) recovers \(T\).  The Radon--Nikodym characterization of conditional expectation then gives, for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
 =g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s).
\]
Division is performed only on \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\).

For Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\), the fixed Radon--Nikodym versions agree with their observed-arm circle integrals.  At every such \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\), consistency yields
\[
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap\mathcal E_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P}
 \mu_{t,P}(z)f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z)}
 {\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap\mathcal E_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P}
 f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z)}.
\]
Since \(q\geq1\), the H\"older condition implies \(|\mu_{t,P}(z)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq L\lVert z-x\rVert_2\).  The ratio is a probability-weighted average over points at distance \(s\), whence
\[
 |g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls
\]
for \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)ds\)-almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  Given \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(r<\varepsilon/L\).  The exceptional set in the defining essential-limit display then has zero radial measure, and the essential-support result prevents the definition from being vacuous.  Hence
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x).
\]
Applying this argument separately to \(t=0\) and \(t=1\), then using the causal definition of \(\tau_P\), gives
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)
 =\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]
No value at a zero-denominator radius and no common sequence of radii has been used.
statements.justification: The lemma makes exact-distance conditioning well posed without asserting that every circle has positive arm density and shows that the canonical representative identifies the boundary contrast.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance, Theorem 1, supplies the identification background; this lemma makes the coarea version and zero-denominator convention explicit under score absolute continuity.
statements.consumer: The two primitive-class frontier theorems use this canonical radial regression for bias and causal interpretation.

statements.statement:
There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The observed arms are the two half-squares; the regressions are disjoint radial \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and actual-arm local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both observed arm-specific radial measures at \(x_j\) agree, their fixed Radon--Nikodym densities therefore agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere, their arm-specific radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and actual-arm local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).
statements.proof_tex:
We construct the family and verify the class, observed-arm, separation, and information properties.  Begin with \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), lower and upper half-square assignment regions, and
\[
 \mathcal B=\{(u-1/2,0):0\leq u\leq1\},
 \qquad \gamma(u)=(u-1/2,0).
\]
The base density is one.  The chart is injective and smooth of every order.  At an endpoint either observed arm contains a quarter disk.  All densities below are at least \(3/4\), so, for \(0<r\leq r_0\leq1/4\),
\[
 P\{T=t,\ X\in B_2(x,r)\}\geq\frac{3\pi}{16}r^2\geq c_-r^2.
\]
Thus actual-arm thickness holds uniformly.

Choose \(\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))\) with \(0\leq\psi\leq1\) and \(\psi(0)=1\), and define the smooth radial bump
\[
 \phi(z)=\psi(\lVert z\rVert_2^2),
 \qquad
 \varphi(r)=\psi(r^2)
\]
Thus \(\phi(z)=\varphi(\lVert z\rVert_2)\), \(0\leq\phi\leq1\), and \(\phi\) is compactly supported in \(B_2(0,1)\).  Put
\[
 \Delta=d a_n,
 \qquad w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q}.
\]
Pack the trimmed interface with centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) separated by at least \(3w\).  For all large \(n\), the radius-\(w\) disks are disjoint and avoid the endpoints, while interval packing gives
\[
 M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Write
\[
 \phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)
 =\varphi(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2/w).
\]
For \(0\leq k\leq q\),
\[
 \lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}
 =C_\phi d_1^{-k/q}\Delta^{1-k/q}.
\]
For \(k\geq1\), this is at most \(C_\phi d_1^{-k/q}\), while for \(k=0\) it is at most \(C_\phi\Delta\).  Disjoint supports give the same derivative bounds for every signed sum.  Choose \(d_1\) large, then choose the affine slope \(b>0\) and \(d>0\) small enough for the fixed H\"older ball.

For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), set
\[
 p_{0,\omega}(z)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 p_{1,\omega}(z)=\frac12+bz_1
 +\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
After decreasing \(b\) and \(d\), these lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), take independent
\[
 Y(t)=B_t+\varepsilon_t,
 \qquad B_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{t,\omega}(z)),
 \qquad \varepsilon_t\sim N(0,1).
\]
Then \(\mu_{t,P_\omega}=p_{t,\omega}\) and \(1\leq\sigma^2_{t,P_\omega}\leq5/4\).  Hoeffding's lemma and the Gaussian moment-generating identity yield
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[e^{\lambda\{Y(t)-p_{t,\omega}(X)\}}\mid X\right]
 \leq e^{\lambda^2/8}e^{\lambda^2/2}
 \leq e^{L^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]

To hide the bump at its center, choose a smooth cutoff \(\chi\) with \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\) and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\).  Fix \(c_A\geq8\), enlarging it later by a constant depending only on \(L\) for the canonical-square construction, and set
\[
 A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\varphi(r/w)}{br}
 \chi\!\left(\frac{br}{c_A\Delta}\right),
\]
with \(A_n(0)=0\).  There is no division at zero because the cutoff vanishes near zero.  On the active region \(br\geq c_A\Delta\), \(|A_n(r)|\leq2/c_A\leq1/4\).  Smooth compact support makes the correction continuous at its outer edge.  Put
\[
 f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j
 A_n(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2)
 \frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2}
 \mathbf1\{z\in B_2(x_j,w)\},
\]
with every summand defined as zero at its center.  The scalar functions \(\varphi(r/w)\) and \(A_n(r)\) are constant on each circle centered at \(x_j\).  Consequently each angular density correction is a radial scalar times \(\cos\theta\), whose integral is zero on each full circle and on each observed half-circle.  This circlewise constancy is the claimed angular cancellation and gives \(\int_Sf_\omega=1\).  Disjointness makes the formula unambiguous, continuous, and bounded in \([3/4,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).  Set \(T=\mathbf1\{X\in\mathcal E_{1,P_\omega}\}\), \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), and sample independently.  This verifies assignment, consistency, iid sampling, compact support, absolute continuity, the density envelopes, H\"older smoothness, sub-Gaussian tails, and actual-arm thickness for every vertex.

Compare adjacent vertices \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{(j)}\), oriented so that \(\omega_j=1\).  On either observed half-circle centered at \(x_j\), the angular integral of \(\cos\theta\) is zero.  Thus their observed arm-specific radial measures coincide, and their fixed RN densities coincide Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  On the treated upper half-circle, the bump value is the circlewise constant \(\Delta\varphi(r/w)\); whenever \(br\geq2c_A\Delta\), \(\chi=1\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega}(x_j+re_\theta)
 \{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
 -\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+re_\theta)\,d\theta\\
 &\qquad=\pi\Delta\varphi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The control equality follows from its constant regression.  A Bernoulli variable followed by the common Gaussian channel is determined, after angular mixing at a fixed radius, by the averaged Bernoulli probability.  Hence the observed radial outcome laws agree outside \(r\leq2c_A\Delta/b\), modulo the immaterial null set of RN representatives.

Inside that interval the common radial density is at most \(Cr\), and the averaged Bernoulli probabilities differ by at most \(C\Delta\) while remaining in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The inequalities
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{KL}(B+\varepsilon,B'+\varepsilon)
 \leq\operatorname{kl}(p,p')
\]
and data processing therefore give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega,x_j},
 P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega^{(j)},x_j})
 \leq C\int_0^{2c_A\Delta/b}\Delta^2r\,dr
 \leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Tensorization yields \(C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n\), whereas
\[
 \log M=\left(\frac1{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choose \(d\) small enough that the divergence is at most \(\alpha\log M\) for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\), retaining slack for Poissonization at mean \(2n\).  At \(x_j\), adjacent targets differ by \(\Delta\phi_j(x_j)=da_n\), so \(c_1=d\) works.

For the canonical square \([-1,1]^2\), use \(\gamma(u)=(2u-1,0)\), base density \(1/4\), and the same relative-density construction.  If \(L>4\), put \(\varepsilon_L=1-4/L>0\), enlarge the cutoff constant depending only on \(L\), and choose \(d_1\) large and then \(d/b\) small.  The relative perturbation is at most \(\varepsilon_L/2\), so
\[
 L^{-1}\leq\frac14(1-\varepsilon_L/2)
 \leq f_\omega\leq\frac14(1+\varepsilon_L/2)\leq L.
\]
All cancellation and divergence bounds change only by constants, placing the family in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).  At \(L=4\), normalization and the floor force density \(1/4\), so the nonzero angular perturbation is unavailable; no such construction is claimed there.
statements.justification: This explicit compressed-experiment construction converts angular-density confounding into the logarithmic uniform lower bound even under a straight interface and smooth regressions.
statements.gap: The published pointwise converse does not distribute continuous angular-density perturbations over separated trimmed-boundary centers with a logarithmic divergence budget.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable, smooth, and strict-slack straight-class distance converses use this contained stronger family.

statements.statement: For every \(q\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,L,c_{-},r_0\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}.\] The upper inequality is attained by the fixed degree-zero triangular-kernel estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\). The lower inequality is supplied by the separated compressed-experiment family in \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\). This theorem concerns the explicitly defined primitive two-sided-thickness class and asserts no inclusion in, or same-class tightening of, the nonparametric class in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the sharp logarithm-bearing uniform frontier for the enlarged primitive two-sided-thickness coordinatewise-distance experiment.
statements.gap: The published lower bound is pointwise in its packing architecture. This theorem obtains the logarithmic factor on a separate class and makes no class-inclusion claim.
statements.consumer: Distance-based boundary analyses receive a rate-sharp bandwidth and worst-case uniform error guarantee under an inspectable arm-mass condition and a bounded score density.
statements.proof_tex:
We first prove achievability.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\), an arm \(t\), a boundary point \(x\), and \(0<h\leq r_0\).  Put \(R_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2\) and
\[
 W_{t,x,h}=h^{-2}\mathbf1\{T=t\}K_\triangle(R_x/h).
\]
The stability lemma gives \(d_{t,P,x}(h)=\mathbb E_PW_{t,x,h}\geq\kappa_0\).  The observed-arm upper-mass lemma, \(0\leq K_\triangle\leq1\), consistency, the H\"older-ball supremum bound, and conditional sub-Gaussianity imply
\[
 \mathbb E_PW_{t,x,h}^2\leq\pi Lh^{-2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\{W_{t,x,h}Y\}^2]\leq Ch^{-2}.
\]
Conditioning on \(X\), for every integer \(k\geq2\), also gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P|W_{t,x,h}\{Y-\mu_{t,P}(X)\}|^k
 \leq k!C^kh^{2-2k}.
\]
Expanding the exponential series and applying exponential Markov inequality yields, for a centered numerator or denominator summand \(Z_{t,x,h}\),
\[
 P\!\left(\left|(\mathbb P_n-P)Z_{t,x,h}\right|>u\right)
 \leq2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{cnu^2}{h^{-2}+h^{-2}u}\right\}.
\]

Cover \(\mathcal B_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\) by an ambient \(\epsilon_n\)-net with \(\epsilon_n=n^{-4}\); its cardinality is at most \(C_Ln^8\), without any geometric regularity of the interface.  For a fixed observation, \(\mathbf1\{T_i=t\}\) is independent of \(x\), while \(x\mapsto K_\triangle(\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2/h)\) is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz.  Normalized denominator and numerator oscillations are therefore at most
\[
 C\epsilon_nh^{-3},
 \qquad C\epsilon_nh^{-3}\mathbb P_n|Y|,
\]
with analogous population bounds.  The strict-sign formula in the declared estimator differs from the observed-arm formula only at \(x=X_i\).  Absolute continuity makes sample scores distinct almost surely, so uniformly over \(x\) this changes a normalized denominator by at most \((nh^2)^{-1}\) and a numerator by at most \((nh^2)^{-1}\max_i|Y_i|\).  The tail and regression envelopes give
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P\max_{i\leq n}|Y_i|^2\leq C\log n,
 \qquad
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(\mathbb P_n|Y|)^2\leq C.
\]
A union bound over the net and the oscillation estimates shows that, for every fixed \(A_0>0\), with probability at least \(1-Cn^{-A_0}\),
\[
 \sup_{t,x}|\mathbb P_nW_{t,x,h}-d_{t,P,x}(h)|
 +\sup_{t,x}|\mathbb P_n(W_{t,x,h}Y)-\mathbb E_P(W_{t,x,h}Y)|
 \leq C\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}\right\}
\]
when \(h\asymp a_n\).

For large \(n\), the right side is below \(\kappa_0/2\).  All empirical denominators are positive and bounded below.  By consistency, the population ratio is a kernel-weighted average of \(\mu_{t,P}(z)\) over the observed arm within distance \(h\), so its bias from \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) is at most \(Lh\).  The ratio identity
\[
 \frac{\widehat r}{\widehat d}-\frac rd
 =\frac{\widehat r-r}{\widehat d}
 +\frac rd\frac{d-\widehat d}{\widehat d}
\]
then gives
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq C\left\{h+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}\right\}.
\]
The canonical observed-distance lemma separately identifies the two essential arm limits with the causal regression values.

On the exceptional event, each arm estimate is zero or a convex combination of outcomes, so the loss is at most \(2\max_i|Y_i|+2L\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and sufficiently large \(A_0\) make its expected contribution negligible.  With \(h\asymp a_n\), all three displayed terms are at most \(Ca_n\).  The estimator is a single measurable member of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\), proving the upper bound.

For the converse, fix an arbitrary fixed-\(n\) rule and induce a marked-Poisson rule before applying the testing inequality: from a mean-\(2n\) marked Poisson sample, retain the \(n\) smallest-mark observations on \(\{N\geq n\}\), apply the fixed-\(n\) rule, and return zero on \(\{N<n\}\).  The retained observations have law \(P^{\otimes n}\), while the failure event has probability at most \(e^{-c n}\) and its target loss is at most \(2L\).  Partition the process into the disjoint cells of the actual-arm hypercube and their complement.  Conditional on the bits, the marked restrictions are independent; the complement is bit independent; and cell \(j\) depends only on bit \(j\).  Midpoint thresholding the induced rule at \(x_j\) gives decoder \(j\), whose own cell is observed only through the marked version of \(U_{n,P}(x_j)\); giving it all other cells and the complement uncompressed only enlarges its information.  Poisson tensorization and the packing slack give divergence at most \(2\alpha\log M_n\), where \(2\alpha<1\).  The coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma yields
\[
 P\{\text{at least one bit is decoded incorrectly}\}\geq\frac12-o(1).
\]
Loss below \(c_1a_n/2\) would decode every bit, so the induced Poisson rule has expected loss at least \(ca_n\).  Its risk is at most the maximal fixed-\(n\) risk plus \(2Le^{-cn}\).  Hence every fixed-\(n\) rule has maximal risk at least \(ca_n-o(a_n)\), and therefore
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}})\geq c_{\mathrm{rect}}a_n.
\]
Division by \(a_n\) and passage to \(\liminf\) and \(\limsup\) prove the theorem.  The hard family lies in this project-defined class; no inclusion in the class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem~6, is used.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0,\delta\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}.\] The upper inequality is attained by \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\) and uses only the first-order continuity implied by \(q\geq1\), arm-specific local mass, and the fixed triangular kernel. The lower inequality is attained by the straight-interface, compact-support hard family in the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\); its regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines, and all of its score densities are bounded and continuous.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates the coordinatewise information bottleneck on a smooth boundary without a density continuity premise.
statements.gap: The published smooth-bias calculation is fixed-law and does not provide a class-uniform higher-order constant under the larger bounded-density class.
statements.consumer: Analysts with a smooth assignment map receive the stable degree-zero distance rule and its sharp uniform bandwidth under bounded density and arm thickness.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  The observed-arm local-constant argument from the primitive theorem applies on \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\).  The stability lemma gives a uniform denominator lower bound, the observed-arm upper-mass lemma bounds a kernel window by \(\pi Lh^2\), and \(q\geq1\) gives bias at most \(Lh\).  An ambient \(n^{-4}\)-net of \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\subseteq[-L,L]^2\) has polynomial cardinality.  The same conditional moment-series calculation, exponential Markov bound, and union bound give an event of probability at least \(1-Cn^{-A_0}\) on which all centered numerators and denominators are bounded by
\[
 C\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}\right\}.
\]

An injective \(C^1\) image of a compact interval is Lipschitz and therefore has planar Lebesgue measure zero.  Score absolute continuity consequently implies that almost surely no sample score lies on \(\mathcal B_P\).  Along the boundary, the strict sign in the estimator equals the observed treatment arm simultaneously for all sample indices.  Reverse triangle inequality and kernel Lipschitz continuity bound the net oscillations by
\[
 Cn^{-4}h^{-3},
 \qquad Cn^{-4}h^{-3}\mathbb P_n|Y|.
\]
At \(h\asymp a_n\) these terms are negligible.  The ratio algebra gives on the good event
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq C\left\{h+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}\right\}.
\]
On its complement, the convex-combination or zero-branch bound and \(\mathbb E_P\max_i|Y_i|^2\leq C\log n\) make the expected contribution negligible.  Balancing at \(h\asymp a_n\) proves
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}})
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}a_n.
\]
Only actual observed-arm thickness is used; there is no density floor or continuity premise and no common chart length, speed, reach, or derivative bound.

For the lower bound use the straight-interface family from the angular packing.  Its observed arms are the two half-squares, its centers lie in the trimmed boundary, and the construction verifies all smooth-class member properties, including actual-arm thickness.  Poissonization, independent cell restrictions, the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma, midpoint decoding, and the marked de-Poissonization argument from the preceding proof yield
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}})
 \geq c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}a_n.
\]
Dividing by \(a_n\) proves the displayed limits.  Smooth assignment geometry alone therefore does not improve the coordinatewise-distance exponent over the displayed bounded-density class.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  On the nonempty canonical class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\),
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
The location upper bound is attained by the named stabilized bivariate degree-\((q-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) from \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}location\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), with
\[
 h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), normalization, the density floor, and the fixed square support force \(f_P=1/4\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently, for \(q>1\), distance compression has the slower exponent in the strict-slack case \(L>4\); the exponents coincide when \(q=1\), and the no-slack normalization case \(L=4\) coincides for every \(q\).
statements.proof_tex:
All constants below may depend on the fixed class parameters, \(q\), and \(\delta\), but not on \(n\) or on \(P\).

\emph{Nonemptiness.}  Let \(X\) be uniform on \([-1,1]^2\), use the prescribed two half-planes and chart, take both regressions constant with values in \((1/4,3/4)\), and let each potential outcome be a Bernoulli variable with the corresponding conditional mean plus an independent standard Gaussian variable.  The density \(1/4\) obeys \(L^{-1}\leq 1/4\leq L\).  Each observed arm contains at least a quarter disk at every interface point, so its mass in a radius-\(r\) boundary ball is at least \(\pi r^2/16\), which is no smaller than \(c_-r^2\).  The regressions belong to every displayed H\"older ball after choosing their constant levels inside the envelope.  Finally, Hoeffding's inequality for the centered Bernoulli variable and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\exp\{\lambda(Y(t)-\mu_{t,P}(X))\}\mid X\right]
 \leq \exp(\lambda^2/8)\exp(\lambda^2/2)
 \leq \exp(L^2\lambda^2/2).
\]
Thus this law is in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).

\emph{Full-location upper bound.}  Write \(r_q\), \(K_2\), \(H_t\), and \(G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}location\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\).  If \(v\neq0\), the polynomial \(u\mapsto v^\top r_q(u)\) cannot vanish on the open half-ball \(H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)\).  Therefore
\[
 v^\top G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}v
 =L^{-1}\int_{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)}K_2(u)
 \{v^\top r_q(u)\}^2\,du>0.
\]
Compactness of the unit sphere in this fixed-dimensional coefficient space gives \(\lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}>0\).  The cutoff in the named estimator is consequently well defined.  Its finite sums are Borel, the minimum eigenvalue is continuous on symmetric matrices, and inversion is continuous on the positive-definite cone; hence the cutoff and zero branch make \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) an element of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\).

For \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\) and all sufficiently small \(h\), the rescaled half-ball \(x+h\{H_t\cap B_2(0,1/2)\}\) lies in the appropriate half-square.  The density floor therefore implies the Loewner inequality
\[
 G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)
 :=\mathbb E_P\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)
 \succeq G^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}.
\]
Put
\[
 b_n(h)=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}.
\]
The bounded kernel, bounded monomial vector, density upper bound, and conditional sub-Gaussian inequality imply, entry by entry and for \(0<u\leq1\),
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left(
 \left|\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right|_{ab}>u
 \right)
 \leq2\exp(-cnh^2u^2),
\]
and
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left(
 \left|\widehat r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right|_a>u
 \right)
 \leq2\exp\{-cnh^2\min(u^2,u)\}.
\]
These displays follow by applying the exponential Markov inequality to the centered summands; their conditional variances are at most \(Ch^2\), and the conditional sub-Gaussian premise bounds every higher exponential moment.  Cover the trimmed line segment by a grid of polynomial cardinality in \(n\), apply the union bound to the finitely many matrix and vector entries, and extend from the grid using the Lipschitz kernel and polynomial basis.  On the event \(n^{-1}\sum_i(1+|Y_i|)\leq C\), the extension error is made smaller than \(b_n(h)\) by a sufficiently fine polynomial grid; the complement has polynomially small probability by the same exponential-moment bound.  Thus, uniformly over the class,
\[
 \sup_{t,x}\left\{
 \left\|\widehat G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-G^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\left\|\widehat r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,x}(h)-r^{\mathrm{loc}}_{t,P,x}(h)\right\|_2
 \right\}=O_P\{b_n(h)\},
\]
with the same order after taking the expected supremum.

Taylor's formula through total degree \(q-1\), using \(\mu_{t,P}\in\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\), writes
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(x+hu)=r_q(u)^\top\beta_{t,P,x}(h)+R_{t,P,x}(u,h),
 \qquad |R_{t,P,x}(u,h)|\leq Ch^q
\]
on the kernel support.  Polynomial reproduction and the population Gram lower bound show that the population fitted intercept differs from \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) by at most \(Ch^q\).  The Rayleigh-quotient perturbation inequality activates the cutoff whenever the preceding Gram deviation is below \(\lambda^{\mathrm{hb}}_{t,q,L}/2\) and bounds the inverse there.  On that event, the resolvent identity
\[
 \widehat G^{-1}-G^{-1}
 =\widehat G^{-1}(G-\widehat G)G^{-1}
\]
and the last two displays give stochastic error \(Cb_n(h)\).  On the active branch the cutoff gives \(|\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h}(x)|\leq Ch^{-2}\mathbb P_n|Y|\), while the failed branch is zero.  Cauchy--Schwarz, the uniform second-moment bound implied by conditional sub-Gaussianity, and the polynomially small exceptional probability make the exceptional contribution negligible.  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\{h^q+b_n(h)\}.
\]
For \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), one has \(b_n(h)\leq Ch^q\), proving the upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\) with the named data-driven estimator.

\emph{Full-location converse.}  Work inside the uniform-design submodel just constructed.  Choose \(M\asymp h^{-1}\) trimmed centers with disjoint radius-\(h\) disks.  Keep the control regression and a constant treated baseline fixed.  In alternative \(j\), add
\[
 \Delta\phi((z-x_j)/h),
 \qquad \Delta=\eta h^q,
\]
to the treated regression, where \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_2(0,1))\), \(0\leq\phi\leq1\), and \(\phi(0)=1\).  For every \(k\leq q\),
\[
 \left\|D^k\{\Delta\phi((\cdot-x_j)/h)\}\right\|_\infty
 \leq C\eta h^{q-k}\leq C\eta.
\]
Thus sufficiently small fixed \(\eta\) places every alternative in the same H\"older ball and keeps its Bernoulli probability away from zero and one.  The common Gaussian-noised Bernoulli channel and the bound
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')}
\]
give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq Cn\Delta^2h^2=C\eta^2nh^{2q+2}.
\]
Take \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), with its constant and then \(\eta\) small enough that the last display is at most \(\alpha\log M\) for some \(\alpha<1/4\).  If \(J\) is uniform on the \(M\) alternatives, the log-sum inequality yields
\[
 I(J;O_{1:n})\leq M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
For every decoder, the entropy identity and the binary-error decomposition give
\[
 \Pr(\widehat J\neq J)
 \geq1-\frac{I(J;O_{1:n})+\log2}{\log M}
 \geq c>0
\]
for all large \(n\).  Uniform estimation error smaller than \(\Delta/3\) identifies the unique perturbed center, so Markov's inequality in reverse through this testing reduction gives
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq c\Delta=cs_{n,q}.
\]

\emph{Distance experiment when \(L>4\).}  The canonical exact-distance-regression lemma gives the armwise bias bound \(|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls\).  The fixed local-constant stability lemma gives a population denominator bounded below, and the upper-mass lemma bounds its variance scale by \(Ch^2\).  Repeating the preceding exponential-Markov, boundary-net, and ratio-stability calculation for the fixed triangular-kernel numerator and denominator yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\{h+b_n(h)\}.
\]
At \(h\asymp a_n\), \(b_n(h)\leq Ch\), so the distance upper bound is \(Ca_n\).  For \(L>4\), the canonical-square family in \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\) lies inside \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\); its densities are continuous, although continuity is not required of every member of that class.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\) to its compressed coordinate experiments shows that uniform error below a fixed multiple of \(a_n\) would decode all packed coordinates with probability tending to one, whereas the lemma bounds that success probability by \(1/2+o(1)\).  Hence
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq ca_n.
\]

\emph{Distance experiment when \(L=4\).}  The fixed square has Lebesgue area four, the score law has total mass one, and the density floor is \(1/4\).  Therefore
\[
 0=1-\int_{[-1,1]^2}\frac14\,dz
 =\int_{[-1,1]^2}\left\{f_P(z)-\frac14\right\}\,dz.
\]
The integrand is nonnegative Lebesgue-almost everywhere, so
\[
 f_P(z)=\frac14
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }z\in[-1,1]^2.
\]
No continuity is used.  This almost-everywhere equality suffices for every expectation and risk because densities differing on a null set induce the same score law.  It also suffices for the fixed radial Radon--Nikodym versions: polar Fubini implies that, for each trimmed \(x\), the circle integral sees the null exceptional set at only a Lebesgue-null set of radii.  Consequently, for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small \(s\),
\[
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\frac{\pi}{4}s.
\]
Thus all expectations, Radon--Nikodym identities, circle identities, and risk bounds used below are unchanged by replacing \(f_P\) with its constant representative \(1/4\).

Taylor expansion of \(\mu_{t,P}\) through total degree \(q-1\), followed by integration over the appropriate half-circle and division by \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\), supplies uniformly bounded coefficients \(b_{t,k,P}(x)\) such that
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{q-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|
 \leq Cs^q
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  This uses only the H\"older remainder \(Cs^q\); the half-circle moments of each Taylor monomial produce the displayed polynomial coefficients.

Instantiate \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) with \(m=q\) and cutoff constant \(c=\pi/4\).  Its population radial Gram matrix is
\[
 \frac1{h^2}\int_0^h K_\triangle(s/h)v_q(s/h)v_q(s/h)^\top
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
 =\frac\pi4 G_q,
\]
where equality holds because changing an integrand on a null set does not change the integral.  The matrix \(G_q\) is positive definite: for \(v\neq0\), the nonzero polynomial \(v^\top v_q(u)\) has only finitely many zeros, while \(uK_\triangle(u)>0\) on \((0,1)\).  The established admissibility lemma places this estimator in \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  The same entrywise exponential inequalities, now for the radial polynomial basis, the same boundary net, polynomial reproduction, and the preceding remainder yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(q),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\{h^q+b_n(h)\}.
\]
At \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), this is at most \(Cs_{n,q}\).

Every coordinatewise distance rule can be implemented from the full sample and known geometry by computing \(D_{P,x,i}\) from \((X_i,T_i)\).  Hence \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) is a restriction of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\), and, for the common loss and law class,
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq cs_{n,q}.
\]
This proves the \(L=4\) distance equivalence.  Finally,
\[
 \frac{q}{2q+2}>\frac14
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q>1.
\]
Thus the strict-slack distance exponent is slower exactly when \(q>1\), the exponents agree at \(q=1\), and the no-slack case agrees for every \(q\), as claimed.
statements.justification: Holding geometry and the causal target fixed reveals the statistical price of releasing only one distance coordinate, and also identifies the no-density-slack exception.
statements.gap: The full-regressor benchmark and location-based boundary theory do not pair their rate with a direct distance-only angular-confounding converse on the identical straight class.
statements.consumer: A data steward can determine whether a distance-only release loses an exponent: it does for \(q>1\) only when \(L>4\), and it does not when \(L=4\).

statements.statement:
Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  This is a conditional risk-transfer theorem.  Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be a subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
\]
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|
 \leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Under exactly these radial hypotheses, zero lies in the essential support of each observed radial measure, \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) equals \((0,r_*]\) modulo a Lebesgue-null set there, and the separate observed arm limits identify \(\tau_P(x)\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently, under those same radial hypotheses,
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If, in addition, \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains for every sufficiently large \(n\) the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted without that containment, and none is asserted for \(m<q\).  Independently, a law class that contains the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate only when the order-one radial hypotheses and that hard-family containment both hold; for every \(m\geq2\), the faster displayed upper rate is asserted only under the order-\(m\) radial hypotheses, and its matching converse additionally requires contained bumps and \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that, for Lebesgue-almost every sufficiently small treated-half-circle radius, a locally constant regression gives a constant normalized-coarea ratio, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives the ratio \(s^{1+\alpha}/2\) for some \(0<\alpha<1\) and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder even in the almost-everywhere sense.  Hence density alone does not determine these examples' joint normalized-coarea remainder; no universal weakest-threshold impossibility is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
All constants below may depend on \(m,q,\iota,L,\delta,A,r_*,\underline c,\overline c\), and the common coefficient bound, but not on \(n\), \(P\), \(t\), or \(x\).  We take the cutoff input suppressed in \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) to be \(c=\underline c\), and take \(h\leq r_*\).

First, the lower radial inequality gives
\[
 \int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\geq\frac{\underline c}{2}r^2>0,
 \qquad 0<r\leq r_*.
\]
It also gives \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\), so \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) equals that interval modulo a null set.  If \(B\) is the common coefficient bound, then the remainder assumption implies
\[
 |g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 \leq B\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}s^k+As^m\longrightarrow0
\]
for almost every such \(s\downarrow0\).  The radial-coarea identification lemma therefore proves the separate essential limits and
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]

We next prove the uniform upper bound.  Put \(v(u)=v_m(u)\), \(G=G_m\), and \(S_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2\).  The arm-specific population matrices and vectors corresponding to the estimator are
\[
 \overline G_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\frac1{h^2}\int_0^hK_\triangle(s/h)v(s/h)v(s/h)^\top
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
\]
and
\[
 \overline r_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\frac1{h^2}\int_{\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\cap(0,h)}
 K_\triangle(s/h)v(s/h)
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
The assumed radial lower bound gives \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,h)\), so the complement of \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\cap(0,h)\) in \((0,h)\) is Lebesgue-null.  By the Radon--Nikodym identities defining \(N_{t,P,x}\) and \(Q_{t,P,x}\), the restricted integral is therefore exactly the population outcome vector corresponding to the estimator.  In particular, no value of the partial regression is used outside \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\).  Changing variables \(s=hu\) and using the almost-everywhere radial bounds gives, in Loewner order,
\[
 \underline cG\preceq\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)
 \preceq\overline cG.
\]
The matrix \(G\) is positive definite: if \(a\neq0\), the polynomial \(a^\top v(u)\) is not zero almost everywhere on \((0,1)\), and hence
\[
 a^\top Ga=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)\{a^\top v(u)\}^2\,du>0.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_{\min}(\overline G_{t,P,x}(h))\geq\underline c\lambda_{\min}(G)\), exactly the population margin used by the declared cutoff.

Define
\[
 \beta_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\bigl(\mu_{t,P}(x),b_{t,1,P}(x)h,\ldots,
 b_{t,m-1,P}(x)h^{m-1}\bigr)^\top.
\]
The polynomial part of the radial expansion equals \(v(s/h)^\top\beta_{t,P,x}(h)\).  Consequently,
\[
 \overline r_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)\beta_{t,P,x}(h)+e_{t,P,x}(h),
\]
where, since \(\lVert v(u)\rVert_2\leq\sqrt m\) on \([0,1]\),
\[
 \lVert e_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert_2
 \leq\frac{A\overline c\sqrt m}{h^2}
 \int_0^h s^{m+1}\,ds
 \leq C h^m.
\]
It follows that the population fitted intercept obeys
\[
 \left|e_1^\top\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)^{-1}
 \overline r_{t,P,x}(h)-\mu_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \leq Ch^m.
\]
This calculation uses only almost-everywhere radial identities; changing a Radon--Nikodym representative on a null set changes none of the integrals.

For completeness, we derive the stochastic order.  For a fixed \(t,x\), each entry of the empirical Gram summand is bounded by \(Ch^{-2}\), and the upper radial inequality gives
\[
 P\{T=t,\ S_x\leq h\}=\int_0^hQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
 \leq\frac{\overline c}{2}h^2.
\]
Hence its variance is at most \(Ch^{-2}\).  Conditional sub-Gaussianity, consistency, and the H\"older-ball supremum bound similarly imply, for every integer \(k\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left|
 h^{-2}\mathbf1\{T=t\}K_\triangle(S_x/h)v_j(S_x/h)Y
 \right|^k
 \leq k!C^kh^{2-2k}.
\]
Centering changes only the constant.  Expanding the exponential series and applying exponential Markov inequality therefore gives, for every scalar Gram or outcome coordinate \(Z_{t,x,h}\),
\[
 P\!\left(\left|(\mathbb P_n-P)Z_{t,x,h}\right|>u\right)
 \leq2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{cnu^2}{h^{-2}+h^{-2}u}\right\}.
\]

The smooth embedded boundary is contained in \([-L,L]^2\).  For \(\epsilon_n=n^{-4}\), it has an \(\epsilon_n\)-net of cardinality at most \(C_Ln^8\), obtained from the ambient square.  A \(C^1\) image of a compact interval is planar-null, so score absolute continuity implies that, with probability one, no sample score lies on \(\mathcal B_P\).  Therefore the strict sign in the estimator equals \(\mathbf1\{T_i=t\}\) simultaneously for every boundary point and sample index.  On \([0,1]\), the finitely many functions
\[
 u\longmapsto K_\triangle(u)v_j(u),
 \qquad
 u\longmapsto K_\triangle(u)v_j(u)v_k(u)
\]
are Lipschitz.  Reverse triangle inequality consequently bounds empirical oscillations between a boundary point and its net point by
\[
 C_m\epsilon_nh^{-3}
 \quad\text{for Gram entries},
 \qquad
 C_m\epsilon_nh^{-3}\mathbb P_n|Y|
 \quad\text{for outcome coordinates},
\]
with the same population bounds.  The conditional tail envelope gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P(\mathbb P_n|Y|)^2\leq C,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\max_{i\leq n}|Y_i|^2\leq C\log n.
\]
A union bound over the fixed matrix dimension, the two arms, and the polynomial net shows that, for every fixed \(A_0>0\), an event \(\mathcal G_n\) of probability at least \(1-Cn^{-A_0}\) exists on which
\[
 \sup_{P,t,x}\left\{
 \lVert\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)-\overline G_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\lVert\widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)-\overline r_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert_2
 \right\}
 \leq C\eta_n(h),
\]
where
\[
 \eta_n(h)=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+\frac{\log n}{nh^2}.
\]
Here and below the supremum notation means that the same constants and probability bound hold uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal C\), not that samples under different laws share one probability space.

For \(h=h_n\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2m+2)}\), \(\eta_n(h_n)\to0\).  Weyl's eigenvalue inequality and the population margin imply on \(\mathcal G_n\), for all large \(n\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h_n))
 \geq\frac12\underline c\lambda_{\min}(G).
\]
Thus every cutoff is active and every empirical inverse is uniformly bounded.  The coefficient vector \(\beta_{t,P,x}(h_n)\) is uniformly bounded, so the inverse identity
\[
 \widehat G^{-1}-\overline G^{-1}
 =\widehat G^{-1}(\overline G-\widehat G)\overline G^{-1}
\]
and the preceding population bias yield
\[
 \sup_{t,x}
 |\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h_n,\underline c}(x)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 \leq C\{h_n^m+\eta_n(h_n)\}
\]
on \(\mathcal G_n\).  On its complement, the admissibility lemma gives
\[
 |\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h_n,\underline c}(x)|
 \leq Ch_n^{-2}\mathbb P_n|Y|,
\]
with zero on the failed-cutoff branch.  Cauchy--Schwarz and the arbitrarily large polynomial exponent \(A_0\) make the exceptional expected contribution \(o(h_n^m)\).  The admissibility lemma also proves that the arm difference belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  Since
\[
 h_n^m\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh_n^2}}\asymp h_n^m,
 \qquad
 \frac{\log n}{nh_n^2}\asymp h_n^{2m},
\]
we obtain
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Taking the infimum over the distance decision class proves the asserted risk upper bound.

We now verify the conditional converse.  Work on the uniform square \([-1/2,1/2]^2\) with the horizontal straight interface, and choose \(M\asymp h_n^{-1}\) trimmed centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) whose radius-\(h_n\) disks are disjoint.  Let \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_2(0,1))\) be radial with \(\phi(0)=1\), put \(\Delta_n=\eta h_n^m\), and keep the control regression zero.  Under the baseline the treated regression is zero, while under alternative \(j\) it is
\[
 \mu_{1,j}(z)=\Delta_n\phi((z-x_j)/h_n).
\]
Take independent standard Gaussian errors in both potential outcomes.  For every derivative order \(k\leq q\),
\[
 \lVert D^k\mu_{1,j}\rVert_\infty
 \leq C\eta h_n^{m-k}\leq C\eta
\]
because \(m\geq q\) and \(h_n\leq1\).  Thus sufficiently small fixed \(\eta\) puts every law in the ambient \(q\)-H\"older and conditional sub-Gaussian class.  In fact the scaled bumps have all derivatives through order \(m\) uniformly bounded, so Taylor's formula and half-circle averaging verify the order-\(m\) normalized-coarea remainder uniformly at every trimmed boundary point.  Uniform design gives \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\pi s\) for all sufficiently small relevant radii.  Hence these are precisely valid contained bump laws of the kind stipulated by the theorem; the extra containment hypothesis places them in \(\mathcal C\).

For the observed full sample, Gaussian relative entropy and the area of a bump support give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac n2\mathbb E\!\left[
 \mathbf1\{T=1\}\mu_{1,j}(X)^2\right]
 \leq Cn\Delta_n^2h_n^2
 =C\eta^2nh_n^{2m+2}.
\]
Now \(nh_n^{2m+2}\asymp\log n\) and \(\log M\sim(2m+2)^{-1}\log n\).  Decreasing \(\eta\) makes the last divergence at most \(\alpha\log M\) for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\).  If \(J\) is uniform on \(\{0,1,\ldots,M\}\), the log-sum inequality gives
\[
 I(J;O_{1:n})
 \leq\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
For any decoder \(\widehat J\), writing \(E=\mathbf1\{\widehat J\neq J\}\) and expanding conditional entropy gives
\[
 H(J\mid O_{1:n})\leq H(E)+P(E)\log M
 \leq\log2+P(E)\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\), the preceding two displays bound \(P(E)\) away from zero.  Uniform estimation error below \(\Delta_n/3\) identifies whether there is no bump or which unique center carries the bump.  Therefore even the full-location minimax risk, and hence the distance-only risk, is at least
\[
 c\Delta_n
 =c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
This proves exactness under the stated containment and \(m\geq q\).  When either condition is absent, this construction supplies no same-class converse, exactly as the theorem records.

Independently, suppose a law class contains the shrinking angular-imbalance hypercube from \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\).  Its separated centers, adjacent compressed divergences, and target gap are those of the angular-density packing lemma.  Given an arbitrary fixed-\(n\) coordinatewise rule, first induce a marked-Poisson rule by retaining the \(n\) smallest-mark observations on \(\{N\geq n\}\), applying the fixed-\(n\) rule there, and using the zero default otherwise.  The retained observations are independent with the original law.  The disjoint bump-cell restrictions of the marked Poisson process are conditionally independent, and midpoint thresholding the induced rule gives the decentralized decoders of the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma.  The packing slack keeps their Poisson divergences below \(2\alpha\log M_n\) with \(2\alpha<1\), so the probability of at least one error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).  Error below half the target separation would decode every bit.  Since \(P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\leq e^{-cn}\) and the zero-default target loss is uniformly bounded on the hard family, the induced Poisson risk is at most the fixed-\(n\) risk plus \(O(e^{-cn})\).  Thus that class has distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  For \(m=1\), the upper exponent is \(1/4\); for \(m\geq2\), the displayed conditional upper exponent is strictly larger.  The converse statements remain limited to the two explicitly contained hard families.

It remains to prove the density example.  Fix \(0<\alpha<1\), take the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\) with horizontal interface through the origin, and define
\[
 f(z)=
 \begin{cases}
 1+\lVert z\rVert_2^{\alpha-1}z_1,&z\neq0,\\
 1,&z=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Because \(|\lVert z\rVert_2^{\alpha-1}z_1|\leq\lVert z\rVert_2^\alpha<1\) on \(S\), this density is bounded, positive, and continuous.  Its second term is odd in \(z_1\), so its integral over \(S\) is zero; since \(S\) has area one, \(f\) integrates to one.  On a treated half-circle of radius \(0<s<1/2\), write \(z=s(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), \(0\leq\theta\leq\pi\).  Then
\[
 f(z)=1+s^\alpha\cos\theta,
 \qquad
 Q_{1,P,0}(s)=s\int_0^\pi(1+s^\alpha\cos\theta)\,d\theta=\pi s.
\]
For a constant regression \(\mu(z)=c\), the radial ratio is identically \(c\).  For the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\), it is instead
\[
\begin{aligned}
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,0}(s)
 &=\frac{s\int_0^\pi s\cos\theta
 (1+s^\alpha\cos\theta)\,d\theta}{\pi s}\\
 &=\frac{s^{1+\alpha}}2.
\end{aligned}
\]
If an order-two expansion existed, some constant \(b_1\) and finite \(A\) would satisfy
\[
 \left|\frac{s^{1+\alpha}}2-b_1s\right|\leq As^2
\]
for almost every sufficiently small \(s\).  Dividing first by \(s\) and sending \(s\downarrow0\) forces \(b_1=0\); dividing then by \(s^2\) would require \(s^{\alpha-1}/2\leq A\), which is impossible because \(\alpha<1\).  Thus the same bounded positive continuous density supports a constant-regression example with an exact constant ratio and an affine-regression example that fails the order-two remainder.  This proves the final claim without asserting any universal weakest density threshold.

statements.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(j\), dominate \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) by their sum and write their densities as \(q_{j,0}\) and \(q_{j,1}\).  The common subprobability measure has density \(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1}\) and mass
\[
 \rho_j=\int(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1})
 =1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Generate the binary compressed experiment by first drawing an ambiguity indicator \(A_j\), independent of \(\Omega_j\), with \(\Pr(A_j=1)=\rho_j\).  On \(A_j=1\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized common submeasure, independently of \(\Omega_j\); on \(A_j=0\), draw it from the normalized residual measure corresponding to \(\Omega_j\).  Zero-mass cases may be assigned arbitrary kernels because their indicators then have probability zero.  Use independent indicators and seeds across \(j\).  Because all observation spaces are standard Borel, a regular conditional kernel for \(Z_j\) given \((S_j,\Omega_j)\) exists; applying it reconstructs the original local experiment.  Independently draw the bit-independent ancillary \(Z_0\) from its fixed law.  The conditional product premise shows that this coupling preserves the joint law of the stated experiment.

Fix the ambiguity indicators, all non-bit seeds, and the bits outside the ambiguous coordinate set \(A=\{j:A_j=1\}\).  If \(A\neq\varnothing\), consider the configurations of \((\Omega_j:j\in A)\) on which every decoder is correct.  Two configurations that differ only at coordinate \(j\in A\) cannot both succeed: decoder \(j\) sees the same \(S_j\), the same \(Z_{-j}\), and the same \(Z_0\) at the two endpoints, so its output is unchanged while the correct bit is reversed.  The successful configurations therefore form an independent set in the \(|A|\)-dimensional hypercube.  Pairing vertices along any coordinate shows that this set has at most \(2^{|A|-1}\) elements.  The ambiguous bits remain uniform, so conditional exact-success probability is at most \(1/2\).  If \(A=\varnothing\), it is at most one.  Averaging proves
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\Pr(A=\varnothing)+\frac12\Pr(A\neq\varnothing)
 =\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]

For the relative-entropy consequence, define the Hellinger affinity \(H_j=\int\sqrt{q_{j,0}q_{j,1}}\).  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_{j,0}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\geq-2\log H_j.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{1-H_j^2}
 \leq\sqrt{1-e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}}.
\]
Since \(1-\sqrt{1-u}\geq u/2\) for \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \rho_j\geq\frac12e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}
 \geq\frac12M^{-\kappa}.
\]
Therefore \(\prod_j(1-\rho_j)\leq\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}=o(1)\), and the preceding exact-success bound implies an any-error probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\geq1\), cutoff constant \(c>0\), bandwidth \(h>0\), law \(P\), and boundary point \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), the rule in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\) is a measurable function of \(U_{n,P}(x)\), and therefore its arm difference is an element of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  Moreover, on the active-cutoff branch,
\[
 \left|\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)\right|
 \leq
 \frac{2\sqrt m}{c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)}h^{-2}
 \left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|\right),
\]
whereas on the failed-cutoff branch the arm intercept is exactly zero.
statements.proof_tex:
All coordinates in the construction are Borel functions of the pairs \((Y_i,D_{P,x,i})\): absolute value and the strict sign indicators are Borel, \(K_\triangle\) and \(v_m\) are continuous, finite sums and products are Borel, the minimum eigenvalue is continuous on the symmetric matrices, and matrix inversion is continuous on the invertible matrices.  The active branch is contained in the set on which the minimum eigenvalue is at least \(c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)/2>0\); the other branch is assigned the fixed value zero.  Thus the piecewise formula is Borel.  It uses only \(U_{n,P}(x)\), including the declared convention when \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), so the definition of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) gives admissibility.

On the active branch, the spectral cutoff gives
\[
 \left\|\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\frac{2}{c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)}.
\]
Because \(0\leq K_\triangle\leq1\) and \(\|v_m(u)\|_2\leq\sqrt m\) on \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \left\|\widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\right\|_2
 \leq\frac{\sqrt m}{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|.
\]
Multiplication by \(e_1^\top\), whose Euclidean norm is one, proves the displayed bound.  The failed-cutoff assertion is exactly the zero convention in the construction.

statements.statement:
For every \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\), there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on \(q\) and \(L\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), there exist \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) points \(x_1,\ldots,x_{M_n}\) on the boundary of the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), separated by at least a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and laws \(P_\omega\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), indexed by \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), with the following properties.  Every law has support \(S\), a continuous density \(f_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq f_{P_\omega}\leq L\), a regression \(\mu_{P_\omega}\) in the stated \(q\)-H\"older ball, and a continuous conditional variance \(\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\leq L\).  The boundary \(\operatorname{bd}(S)\) is rectifiable and the observations are independently and identically distributed.  If \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs from \(\omega\) only in coordinate \(j\), then
\[
 \left|\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)-\mu_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\right|\geq c_1a_n,
\]
the laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree, the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\) and use its lower edge.  All centers below lie in the relative interior of that edge, so a sufficiently small circle centered at \(x_j\) meets \(S\) in the upper half-circle
\[
 x_j+r e_\theta,\qquad e_\theta=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta),
 \qquad 0\leq\theta\leq\pi.
\]
The identities that drive the construction are
\[
 \int_0^\pi\cos\theta\,d\theta=0,
 \qquad
 \int_0^\pi\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac\pi2.
\]

Choose \(\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))\) with \(0\leq\psi\leq1\) and \(\psi(0)=1\), set
\[
 \phi(z)=\psi(\lVert z\rVert_2^2),
 \qquad \varphi(u)=\psi(u^2),
\]
and let
\[
 \Delta=d a_n,
 \qquad w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q}.
\]
Choose points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) on a fixed middle subinterval of the lower edge, separated by \(3w\).  The half-discs \(B_2(x_j,w)\cap S\) are disjoint and avoid the corners for all large \(n\), and elementary interval packing gives
\[
 M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Write \(r_j(z)=\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2\) and \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).

Fix a small affine slope \(b>0\).  For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), define
\[
 p_\omega(z)=\frac12+bz_1+\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
For every integer \(0\leq k\leq q\),
\[
 \lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}.
\]
The right side is bounded by a constant made arbitrarily small at \(k=q\) by increasing \(d_1\), and it tends to zero for \(k<q\).  Disjoint supports preserve these bounds for the sum.  We first choose \(b\) small, then \(d_1\) large, and finally \(d\) small.  This places every \(p_\omega\) in \(\mathcal H^q(S,L)\) and in \([1/4,3/4]\).

Let \(\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) satisfy \(0\leq\chi\leq1\), \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\), and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\).  With a fixed \(c_A\geq8\), define
\[
 A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\varphi(r/w)}{br}
 \chi\!\left(\frac{br}{c_A\Delta}\right),
 \qquad A_n(0)=0.
\]
There is no singularity: the cutoff makes \(A_n\) identically zero on a neighborhood of zero.  On its active region, \(|A_n(r)|\leq2/c_A\leq1/4\), and the compact support of \(\varphi(r/w)\) makes it vanish smoothly before \(r=w\).  Define, relative to the compact support \(S\),
\[
 f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j A_n(r_j(z))
 \frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{r_j(z)}\mathbf1\{r_j(z)<w\},
\]
with each summand set to zero at \(x_j\).  The supports are disjoint, so \(f_\omega\) is unambiguous and continuous on \(S\), including at the centers and support edges.  It lies in \([3/4,5/4]\), which is contained in \([L^{-1},L]\) because \(L\geq4\).  Polar integration over each affected half-disc gives
\[
 \int_0^w A_n(r)r\,dr\int_0^\pi\cos\theta\,d\theta=0.
\]
Thus \(\int_S f_\omega=1\).  Positivity makes \(S\) the support, and the square boundary is a rectifiable curve of finite length.

Conditional on \(X=z\), let
\[
 Y=B+\varepsilon,
 \qquad B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_\omega(z)),
 \qquad \varepsilon\sim N(0,1),
\]
with \(B\) and \(\varepsilon\) conditionally independent.  Then
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(z)=p_\omega(z),
 \qquad
 \sigma^2_{P_\omega}(z)=1+p_\omega(z)\{1-p_\omega(z)\}.
\]
The variance is continuous and belongs to \([1,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).  Taking \((Y_i,X_i)\) independently with this common law verifies, one by one, all four defining conditions of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\): independently and identically distributed sampling; a continuous density on the compact support \(S\subseteq[-L,L]^2\) with the displayed envelope and rectifiable boundary; the \(q\)-H\"older regression envelope; and the continuous conditional-variance envelope.

Fix adjacent vertices, oriented so that \(\omega_j=1\) and \(\omega_j^{(j)}=0\).  Other perturbations vanish in the \(j\)-th half-disc.  At every \(0<r<w\), the density difference integrates to zero on the half-circle, so the two radial densities agree and equal \(\pi r\).  The difference between their outcome-weighted angular integrals is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\int_0^\pi p_\omega(x_j+re_\theta)
       \{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
 -\int_0^\pi p_{\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+re_\theta)\,d\theta\\
 &=\pi\Delta\varphi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r).
\end{aligned}
\]
The terms involving the constant part of the affine regression and the product of the radial bump with \(A_n(r)\cos\theta\) vanish by the first angular identity.  When \(br\geq2c_A\Delta\), the cutoff equals one and the last display is zero.  For \(r\geq w\), both the density and regression perturbations vanish.  Therefore the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside \(r\leq2c_A\Delta/b\): a mixture of Bernoulli variables is Bernoulli with its averaged success probability, and convolution with the common Gaussian noise preserves equality.

On the exceptional interval, the common radial density is \(\pi r\), the two averaged Bernoulli probabilities remain in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their difference is at most \(C\Delta\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')}
 \leq C\Delta^2.
\]
Data processing through addition of the common Gaussian and integration over the common radial marginal yield for one observation
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{rad}}_{\omega,j},P^{\mathrm{rad}}_{\omega^{(j)},j})
 \leq C\Delta^2\int_0^{2c_A\Delta/b}r\,dr
 \leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Independent-product tensorization gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}\right)
 \leq C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \log M=\left(\frac1{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choose \(d\) sufficiently small that the preceding divergence is at most \(\alpha\log M\) for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\), with enough slack for the later Poissonization at mean \(2n\).  Finally, \(\phi_j(x_j)=1\), so adjacent regressions differ at \(x_j\) by \(\Delta=da_n\).  This proves the lemma with \(c_1=d\).

To summarize the membership verification, every vertex and every sufficiently large \(n\) satisfies each of the four conditions in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\): condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\) holds by the independent product construction; condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\) holds because \(S\) is compact with rectifiable boundary and \(f_\omega\) is continuous, normalized, supported on \(S\), and lies between \(L^{-1}\) and \(L\); condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\) is the derivative-scaled \(q\)-H\"older calculation for \(p_\omega\); and condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\) follows from the continuous formula \(\sigma^2_{P_\omega}=1+p_\omega(1-p_\omega)\in[1,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).

Fix \(n\) large enough for the packing lemma and abbreviate \(M=M_n\) and \(\Delta=c_1a_n\).  Let \(\widehat\mu_n\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) be an arbitrary fixed-\(n\) rule.  We first construct from it a marked-Poisson rule, and only then invoke the product lower bound.

Generate a Poisson point process of mean \(2n\) from a packing law \(P_\omega\), and attach independent marks with a continuous distribution to its points.  If its count \(N\) is at least \(n\), retain the \(n\) points with the smallest marks and apply \(\widehat\mu_n\) to those retained observations; if \(N<n\), return the identically zero boundary function.  Call the resulting random-size rule \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}\).  Selection by marks is independent of the observations.  Conditional on \(N=k\geq n\), the retained observations therefore have law \(P_\omega^{\otimes n}\), and the construction is independent of \(P_\omega\).  At each boundary point \(x\), its output uses the retained marked pairs \((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2)\), so it is a coordinatewise rule in the marked compressed experiment.

Partition the Poisson process into the disjoint half-disc cells supporting the bumps and their complement.  Conditional on the independent uniform bits \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\), Poisson restrictions to these sets are independent; cell \(j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\), and the complement is bit independent.  For center \(x_j\), threshold \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x_j)\) at the midpoint of the two possible values of \(\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)\).  This gives a decoder of \(\Omega_j\).  In cell \(j\), the decoder uses only the marked compression \((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x_j\rVert_2)\).  Giving it the marked uncompressed restrictions of all other cells and of the complement can only make decoding easier.  Thus the enlarged experiment has the conditional product form of \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\).  The marks are bit independent and contribute zero relative entropy.

Poisson tensorization multiplies the one-observation relative entropy by \(2n\).  The slack fixed in the packing proof gives, for every \(j\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})
 \leq 2\alpha\log M,
 \qquad 2\alpha<1.
\]
The direct-product lemma consequently yields
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one coordinate is decoded incorrectly}\}
 \geq\frac12-o(1).
\]
Because the regression value at \(x_j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\), uniform loss smaller than \(\Delta/2\) makes every midpoint decoder correct.  Hence the marked-Poisson maximal risk of the induced rule over the finite family is at least
\[
 \frac{\Delta}{2}\left(\frac12-o(1)\right)\geq c a_n.
\]

We now compare that risk with the risk of the original fixed-\(n\) rule.  Since the retained sample has law \(P_\omega^{\otimes n}\) on \(\{N\geq n\}\), and every packing regression is bounded by one, the zero default has loss at most one and
\[
 \sup_\omega \mathbb E_{P_\omega}
 \left[\left\|\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}-\mu_{P_\omega}\right\|_{\infty,\operatorname{bd}(S)}\right]
 \leq
 \sup_\omega \mathbb E_{P_\omega}
 \left[\left\|\widehat\mu_n-\mu_{P_\omega}\right\|_{\infty,\operatorname{bd}(S)}\right]
 +\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}.
\]
The Poisson Chernoff bound gives \(\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\leq e^{-c'n}=o(a_n)\).  Combining the last two displays proves, for every fixed-\(n\) rule,
\[
 \sup_\omega \mathbb E_{P_\omega}
 \left[\left\|\widehat\mu_n-\mu_{P_\omega}\right\|_{\infty,\operatorname{bd}(S)}\right]
 \geq c a_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), after reducing \(c\) if necessary.  The packing proof verified conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(iv)}\) of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) for every member and every sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus the supremum over the full CTY class is no smaller.  Taking the infimum over the inherited law-independent decision class gives \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\geq ca_n\).  Division by \(a_n\) and passage to the lower limit prove the displayed inequality and its equality with the expanded definition of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\).

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the fixed observable radial Radon--Nikodym versions satisfy, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 P\{T=t,\ 0<\lVert X-x\rVert_2\leq r\}
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds,
\]
and agree with the corresponding observed-arm circle integrals for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\).  Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\), so the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) recovers the treatment arm almost surely.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
If zero lies in the essential support of each arm-specific radial measure and the two separate essential limits satisfy \(\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P}(x)=\mu_{t,P}(x)\), then
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)
 =\tau_P(x).
\]
In particular, the almost-everywhere radial lower bound and normalized-coarea remainder in \(\mathrm{thm:angular\text{-}remainder\text{-}transition}\) imply these premises arm by arm.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and write \(R_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2\).  By the definitions of the observable radial measure and its fixed Radon--Nikodym version,
\[
 P\{T=t,\ 0<R_x\leq r\}
 =\nu_{t,P,x}((0,r])
 =\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds
\]
for every \(r>0\).  The polar coarea identities in the definitions of \(Q_{t,P,x}\) and \(N_{t,P,x}\) give agreement with the respective observed-arm circle integrals outside a Lebesgue-null set of radii.  These are almost-everywhere statements about the fixed versions, not pointwise identities at exceptional radii.

Score absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\).  Hence \(R_x>0\) almost surely and
\[
 \operatorname{sgn}(D_{P,x})=2T-1
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
For every bounded Borel function \(a\), the two Radon--Nikodym definitions yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(R_x)]
 =\int_0^\infty a(s)N_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(R_x)]
 =\int_0^\infty a(s)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
The H\"older and conditional sub-Gaussian member properties imply \(\mathbb E_P|Y|<\infty\).  The Radon--Nikodym characterization of conditional expectation, together with sign recovery, therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
 =g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\).  The quotient is used only where \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\).

Now suppose zero is in the essential support in both arms and the two separate essential limits equal their respective boundary regressions.  Applying the definition of \(\tau_P\) gives
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P}(x)-\ell^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P}(x)
 =\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]
Finally, under the radial hypotheses displayed in the transition theorem,
\[
 \int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\geq\frac{\underline c}{2}r^2>0,
 \qquad 0<r\leq r_*,
\]
and \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(s\in(0,r_*]\).  Thus zero is in essential support and \(\mathcal S_{t,P,x}\) agrees with \((0,r_*]\) modulo a null set.  If \(B\) uniformly bounds the displayed coefficients, the normalized-coarea remainder gives
\[
 |g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 \leq B\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}s^k+As^m\longrightarrow0
\]
outside a null set as \(s\downarrow0\).  This proves each separate essential limit and hence all stated identification conclusions.

sampling_model.design: A boundary discontinuity design with a known binary assignment partition of a compact bivariate score support.
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has probability mass at least \(c_{-}r^2\) in every boundary ball of radius \(r\) for \(0<r\leq r_0\); \(f_P\leq L\) yields the derived upper estimate \(\pi Lr^2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The score density is bounded and continuous but has no class-uniform derivative or continuity modulus. Exact-distance regressions use the canonical coarea ratio on positive-denominator radii and the H\"older regression representative on zero-denominator radii. Both distance upper bounds use the fixed triangular kernel and degree zero; the comparison experiment permits estimators to use full score locations jointly.
